messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A bench with harmless scraps and offcuts; then the clutter is untidy without blocking any work. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "I scrape a bright edge with my thumbnail. \"I mark it wrong,\" I say. I rub the scrap, then put it back. I scrape another edge, then leave it crooked. I mark again, then put it back."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i touch the scrap. i look at the offcut. i put the bench beside the scrap. the clutter stays. i put the offbeat in the step. the bench stays dirty."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i hold the scrap against the bench and move it two centimeters. “i did not,” i say. “i removed the part that made me untidy.” i do not touch the rest. the clutter seems to move. i keep my hand off the scrap."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i put the scraps on the bench and mark the cut with pencil. then i put the bench beside it. the clutter stays. i leave the scrap where i found it and leave the paper folded. the work can wait."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I photograph the pile and leave it. My hand knocks the offcut against the bench frame. My thumb slips and the scraps slide under it. I pull the bench back and photograph the pile again. Sorry—sorry, i’m checking whether i’ve moved anything."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i lay the scrap beside the bench and sweep the offcuts with my thumb. then i turn the bench once and mark the scrap with chalk. \"i will leave this scrap here,\" i say, though i keep the mark."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "I tap the bench once and leave the scrap beside it. I turn the bench once and tap the offends once. I set the bench beside the pile and move the scrap once."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "\"scraps. offcut. no—one—\" I check the watch. \"one fold. likely.\" I leave the scraps and offcuts alone."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i write ‘scrap, offcut, and off’ on the bench, then leave it alone. i check the offcuts, find one, and write ‘that one’ on the scrap. i leave the clutter alone, then write ‘that one’ on the bench.’"}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i touch the scraps once, then stop. one goes crooked, so i put it back in the corner. i write the wrong name on the bench beside it, then put the rest in the drawer. the clutter stays tidy, but now i can see the scraps from a different angle."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i leave the scraps where they fell and mark the bench’s edge with grease. i leave the offcuts visible, but i keep the broken part visible so i can see where the clutter moves. if the bench stays tidy, i leave the mark and keep the scraps in place."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i tap the bench with my thumb. “not useful,” i say. i leave the scraps on the table. “one piece, maybe.” i move one bolt into the corner. “touch it first.”"}]
